primary_question: Is the current twelve-deck HSConfig proof set broad enough to catch the common failure modes across aggro, combo, weapon, discard, treant/token, hero-power, mech, boar/combo, pirate, big-minion, and low-curve Warrior shells without bloating the representative matrix?
source_backed_claims: The live proof set is twelve decks total: eleven representative rows in `archetype-fixture-matrix.json` plus supplemental `CuteWarrior` in `supplemental-proof-decks.json`, and `test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py` runs all twelve through the load-safe prepare path.

Every shell family named in this audit is exercised by at least one current deck: ShadowPriest covers aggro and hero-power transform; Boarlock covers combo and boar/combo with `Combo.json`; Kingslayer and PirateRogue cover weapon pressure; Discolock covers discard; TreantDruid covers treant/token; ImbueMage covers hero-power plus generation and discover adjacency; MechPala covers mech; PirateRogue and PirateDH cover pirate pressure; BigShaman covers big-minion cheat; CuteWarrior covers the low-curve Warrior shell.

The current set already exercises the major HSConfig runtime-shape failure lanes for these shells: exact deck identity and per-card CardID emission across all decks, optional `Combo.json` emission only for the combo control row, warning-visible but still load-safe source-informed rows through Kingslayer and Boarlock, and sideboard-aware deck decoding through MechPala.

Kingslayer and Boarlock are intentionally preserved as `source_informed_valid_fixture` rows with explicit stop conditions, so the matrix already checks that HSConfig can stay technically valid and load-safe even when exact guide depth is still blocked.

CuteWarrior remains supplemental rather than representative, but it now has dedicated load-safe proof in `test_supplemental_cute_warrior_load_safe.py` and participates in the universal twelve-deck no-block matrix, which means the low-curve Warrior family is covered without widening the representative matrix.

The repeatedly declared matrix limits are reactive control depth and discover-chain depth, not any missing aggro, combo, weapon, discard, treant/token, hero-power, mech, boar/combo, pirate, big-minion, or low-curve Warrior shell.
unknown_or_blocked_claims: The current proof set does not include a dedicated representative row whose main purpose is secret-heavy freeze or discover-chain pressure, overload-first timing, or location-heavy reactive control.
The repo does not prove that adding one of those beyond-scope families now would catch a more common failure mode than the current twelve-deck set for the shell list in this item.

Kingslayer still exposes an exact Quick Pick mulligan stop condition, and Boarlock still exposes an exact Fracking mulligan stop condition plus remaining runtime-surface blockers, so both rows prove honest warning-path behavior rather than fully closed source-backed strength.
hearthstone_semantics_implications: For shell-level stress, the set is broad enough. It spans burst aggro, board-flood recruit, pirate tempo from both weapon-led and hero-attack-led variants, exact combo sequencing, discard mutation, token snowball, hero-power transform and hero-power use, mech magnetic scaling, big-minion cheat, and low-curve Warrior load-safe generation. Those semantics map directly to the common HSConfig failure modes that matter before runtime: wrong mulligan posture, missing or misrouted per-card runtime blocks, wrong attack or hero-power surfaces, accidental `Combo.json` emission or omission, or deck identity loss. The current decks hit all of those lanes at least once, and several lanes twice from different semantic angles.
hsconfig_current_fit: The current HSConfig design fits this matrix well. The representative matrix stays lean at eleven rows for source-depth truth, while the broader no-block shell proof set reaches twelve total decks by keeping CuteWarrior supplemental. That split is appropriate: the representative rows prove broad archetype and runtime-family coverage, Kingslayer and Boarlock prove blocked-but-load-safe warning behavior, and CuteWarrior proves a narrow low-curve Warrior acceptance lane without distorting matrix governance. The active docs and tests align with this design, so the matrix is doing useful work instead of carrying decorative breadth.
no_block_contract_implications: For the named shell families, the no-block contract is already adequately stressed. A valid deck in these shells should still generate `GlobalValues.json`, `Mulligan.json`, and per-card CardID files; only Boarlock currently needs exact `Combo.json`; Kingslayer and Boarlock show that unresolved source depth remains warning-visible rather than runtime-write-blocking when the package stays load-safe; and CuteWarrior shows that a low-curve Warrior shell can remain supplemental but still be technically covered by the universal no-block proof. The next guard is not another shell deck. The right guard is to keep rerunning the current twelve-deck universal matrix whenever runtime-surface or package-validation logic changes.
lean_architecture_risk: The main risk is matrix bloat through duplication. Another aggro, pirate, weapon, or Warrior row would mostly repeat families that are already covered. Promoting CuteWarrior into the representative matrix without a documented missing family would make the matrix larger but not sharper. Adding a second combo-only or second discard-only row would also dilute attention from the two existing source-informed controls that already expose the hardest honest warning-path edges. The lean rule should stay unchanged: add a new representative deck only when it surfaces a runtime family or source-depth failure that none of the current twelve proof decks can already reveal.
recommended_next_actions: Keep the representative matrix at eleven rows and the broader shell proof set at twelve total decks.
Use the current twelve-deck set as the default shell stress matrix for no-block audits and runtime-surface regression checks.
Do not add a new deck now. The next non-bloating addition count for the shell families in this item is zero.

If a future matrix review expands beyond this shell list, justify any new deck only by a proven uncovered family such as dedicated secret or discover-chain pressure, overload-first timing, or location-heavy reactive control, not by ladder popularity or deck novelty.
